milestones.title: Foundation and discovery
milestones.delivered: Original articles, six topics, search, reading lists and a selected timeline.
milestones.next: Continue to maintain links, accessibility and source attribution.

milestones.title: Unified site-wide navigation
milestones.delivered: Explore, Scripture, Research and Project menus expose every major public hub on desktop and mobile. Source/accessibility audit is exposed under Research; disclosure-group scripting now handles the whole menu collection and closes on focus leaving a group.
milestones.next: Verify keyboard and touch behaviour on physical devices, and test focus management through navigation changes on screen readers.

milestones.title: Biblical primary-text collection
milestones.delivered: Local Bible reader, named-reference index and 26 original guides with explicit passage references.
milestones.next: Add careful textual comparison and qualified specialist review where applicable.

milestones.title: Encyclopaedia expansion and preservation
milestones.delivered: Expanded the original collection with 14 specialist-sourced, independently authored historical guides covering eight rulers, governance, deportation, religion, languages, the imperial collapse and later regional history. Added 56 section-level reading trails, 10 source records and dated timeline routes. Earlier preserved reference corpus, glossary and measured growth dashboard remain available. Added another eight original language and heritage studies without importing unlicensed texts. Six further original methods and community-heritage studies now complement ancient history and linguistic resources. Milestone 9 adds eight long-form Bible-primary, object-identified comparisons (40 precisely mapped new sections), six curated specialist and museum reference records and a public evidence dossier reading hub. The release also connects the new studies to older Bible and history entries. Nine additional Middle Assyrian social-history guides provide 45 sourced sections and a period-sensitive non-royal reading pathway.
milestones.next: Deepen object-level Middle Assyrian administrative and household case studies, with named tablet editions and independent philological review. Extend historical coverage to the transitions between Middle and Neo-Assyrian periods.

milestones.title: The Middle Assyrian world and everyday life
milestones.delivered: Published nine original source-mapped guides with 45 substantive editorial sections about Middle Assyrian provincial administration, law, women, households, fields, irrigation, livestock, dependent labour, ration lists, scribal archives, sealings, religion and exchange. Added ten externally attributed specialist source records, fourteen anchored claim reviews, a public research hub, reciprocal reading routes and a non-royal timeline entry. Legal prescriptions are distinguished from practice; Old and Neo-Assyrian and biblical comparisons are explicitly dated and limited.
milestones.next: Invite qualified Assyriologists to review tablet and legal paragraph translations, precise administrative titles, provenance and dates. Expand dated individual tablet case studies and material culture where object-level research permits; document more non-elite and women's perspectives without inventing identities or experiences. Check rights before using photos, manuscripts or audio.

milestones.title: Interactive historical atlas
milestones.delivered: The interactive historical atlas has eleven dated teaching stages with preserved offline basemap data, timeline playback, modern geography and city context. Milestone 3 adds chapter-specific reconstruction limits, source-by-source scope notes, clearer differentiation of provincial control from vassalage or temporary military reach, 21 linked historical and biblical reading routes, and checks that keep map citations and article links current.
milestones.next: Continue specialist cartographic and historical review before refining polygon coordinates. Map individual provinces only when dated inscriptional, administrative and archaeological evidence supports them. Test real browser behaviour, reduced-motion support and mobile readability. No numerical border certainty or ancient area estimates are justified.

milestones.title: Section-level source traceability
milestones.delivered: Evidence Register, source-to-guide links and 298 section-level evidence trails across 86 editorial guides, including 24 new heritage and community research sections.
milestones.next: Connect more claims to exact individual cuneiform tablet IDs and publication lines. Existing source-to-section links are reading routes, not completed specialist verification.

milestones.title: Historical claim verification
milestones.delivered: The claim-level review register now contains 41 text-anchored records, including twenty-six new biblical and historical-record claims, including fourteen Middle Assyrian social-history claims linked to eight research dossiers. Passage coordinates, direct-vs-context source roles and review limitations are validated; no independent specialist reviews have been claimed.
milestones.next: Arrange documented independent Assyriological, legal-history and biblical-review assessments for 41 outstanding text-anchored records, especially Middle Assyrian legal versus actual practice and period chronology. Maintain no implied peer-review completion.

milestones.title: Assyrian languages and cultural heritage
milestones.delivered: Added eight original specialist-sourced guides with 32 section reading trails on cuneiform interpretation, Syriac manuscript hands and Unicode, local NENA dialects, Urmi documentation, Surayt and ethical recording. A new navigable language reference room presents 22 Unicode-identified Syriac letters, links to HMML manuscript lessons and Cambridge field recordings for Urmi, Alqosh and Ankawa. No third-party audio or protected manuscript images are copied.
milestones.next: Invite qualified speakers and palaeographers to review word forms and transcriptions, then add permission-cleared dialect-labelled pronunciation samples and transliteration conventions. Test Syriac font rendering across devices. Do not claim one universal pronunciation or conflate Akkadian with Neo-Aramaic.

milestones.title: Community testimony and heritage media
milestones.delivered: Launched a public heritage and oral-history reference room containing ten previously published, externally linked records across migration, community institutions, cultural practice and living speech. Added six original method and history guides with 24 source-mapped sections, three blank downloadable planning worksheets, a locally filtered source index and explicit rights, narrator consent and privacy safeguards. No family submissions or protected recordings have been collected or published.
milestones.next: Establish a separately authorised custodian, secure intake and informed-consent review process before collecting personal testimony. Invite community and subject specialists, document narrator review and access restrictions, and add village-specific sourced entries and permission-cleared media only after the needed agreements exist.

milestones.title: Secure contribution delivery
milestones.delivered: Dormant backend is retained and public contributions remain download-only.
milestones.next: Do not imply a working private corrections inbox or media-intake workflow. Authorise a protected, staffed delivery service before taking personal reports, promising responses or storing consent records.

milestones.title: Editorial governance and revision history
milestones.delivered: Published a public editorial governance and revision room, correction/clarification/withdrawal policy, defined role disclosures, two blank release and correction planning documents, and a validated register of nine merged major milestones (including governance, stewardship, source/accessibility, historical evidence and Middle Assyrian life) with their actual merged commits and pull request links. No independent reviewers have been assigned or claimed, and no confirmed public correction notices have been fabricated. Existing article and local correction-draft flows now link to the policy.
milestones.next: Appoint qualified subject editors and documented independent reviewers, create secure private correction intake and tracked moderation, and record genuine dated public correction or withdrawal notices and multilingual revisions when required. The curated ledger must follow subsequent substantive merged changes; CI does not imply specialist review.

milestones.title: Source integrity and accessibility audit
milestones.delivered: Added an offline structural audit for 89 curated institutional source URLs, a separate bounded monthly/manual HTTP health workflow with inconclusive 403/429/timeout handling, a public audit and metadata report, representative-page accessibility markup checks, and automated test coverage. Repaired multi-menu keyboard disclosure handling, improved focus and reduced-motion CSS, and introduced nonvisual atlas chapter status announcements. These checks do not claim real browser testing, all-source remote verification or full WCAG conformance.
milestones.next: Review actual remote health reports with source custodians before changing citations; extend coverage to preserved reference URLs and all generated pages. Record and fix results of keyboard-only, screen-reader, zoom/reflow, contrast/touch-target and Syriac shaping tests on real devices. Keep publication indexing disabled until rights and specialist approvals are granted.

milestones.title: Publication and long-term stewardship
milestones.delivered: Added a dedicated public publication and preservation room, deterministic SHA-256 fixity manifest covering generated files, strict missing/extra/tampered-file verification, recoverable deterministic ZIP export with tested extraction, CI negative tests and restore checks for build and Pages deployment, plus selected live-file hash probes and an operational recovery runbook. Existing noindex safeguards remain unchanged.
milestones.next: Assign a backup custodian and establish independent offsite copies and restoration drills. Use the new source and accessibility audit procedures to review remote citations and real-device WCAG 2.2 usability before any indexing approval. Rights, specialist historical/linguistic review and live publisher availability still require human checks.
